entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 24_Themis_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 2978 vertices and 5952 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 208 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (146°, 73°), period 8.374187 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 103.8031274924952 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The deconvolved camera-1 frames under https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/24Themis/ are now qualified and cast: their pixels carry the survey's own deconvolution, their geometry is computed from the release's rotation record and pinned Horizons tables at each exposure midpoint, and measured coverage is 84.9 percent of the retained surface area with level matching inside gains of 0.91 to 2.74. The reduced Red/ products are not used. This is photographed illumination, not a calibrated global reflectance map, so the missing-imagery grid still marks unphotographed, grazing and rejected surface.

entries.subject: Released SAGE companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 24_Themis.obj, which the imported ledger omitted. Its existence establishes a numerical candidate; method, calibration and independence from the selected MPCD reconstruction still need comparison.
entries.revisitWhen: The SAGE companion’s paper, scale and shape constraints have been compared with the selected MPCD release.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: All 30 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1) are cast as a photograph lens. The registration stage places the body by its outline: 30 of 30 frames project an outline elongated enough to define a position angle, between 1.227 and 1.328, and their limb residual leaves 1.65 degrees after removing the 3.58-degree floor that exposures minutes apart set, so the lens registers. The two sweeps that need surface markings find none: the cross-frame test is decisive on 2 of 30 frames, and the relief sweep's 11 decisive frames disagree among themselves from -9.5 to +9.5 degrees, so their -8.25-degree median reaches no verdict. The column order of the rotation record is settled twice: 145.9511 degrees cannot be a latitude, and both columns match the pole of DAMIT model 5916.
